prov_lang_dao.name: Lãng Đào
prov_lang_dao.lore: Low wooded ground at the river mouth around the gate of hulls of Lãng Đào Môn. Its people are ferrymen, rope-tarrers and boat-builders who carry the river trade for Tùng Đào. On the shore stand the wrecked piers of Phá Chu Trấn, whose feuding boatmen were the reason the ferrymen banded together in 790.

prov_p108.name: Tuyết Ốc
prov_p108.lore: River forest on the upper river, where the snow lies so deep that the houses of Tuyết Ốc Thôn are built half under it. Its people trap, fish and dig snow tunnels door to door all winter. Behind the village lies a forest where the drifts are deeper than a man is tall.

prov_p109.name: Hàn Mai
prov_p109.lore: Wide river forest around Hàn Mai Thôn and its plum. Its people farm the river flats, fish and gather wild plums from the woods. Since 1105 the swordsmen of Ngạo Tuyết Phái have trained in the plum wood above the village.

prov_p110.name: Bạch Lang
prov_p110.lore: River forest around the old den of the white wolf king that Thôi Khinh Hồng slew. Its people hunt, fish and lime the den's boulders white each spring. Grey wolves still prowl a knoll nearby, and the village watches them closely.

prov_p33.name: Đào Thanh
prov_p33.lore: River land and steep forest around Đào Thanh Thành, the busiest city on the river. Timber merchants, river traders and the families of Tùng Đào's outer disciples live here. A spirit vein above the city hums with the pine waves.

prov_p47.name: Đào Sa
prov_p47.lore: Sand flats, bog and forest at the river mouth, around the stilt market of Đào Sa Thị. Its people wash gold, fish and work the landing. A poplar wood holds the dunes behind the flats.

prov_p62.name: Hà Bạn
prov_p62.lore: River forest around Hà Bạn Trấn and its herb mills, which answer to Thải Chi Cốc. Its people fish, grind herbs and ship them downriver. Upslope lie the silted streets of Cựu Hà Trấn, left dry when the river changed course.

prov_p63.name: Lâm Hạ
prov_p63.lore: Shaded beech and pine forest around the granary town of Lâm Hạ Trấn. Its people are granary-keepers, coopers and rat-catchers. The giant rats of a knoll nearby are the reason the granaries stand on stone staddles.

prov_thai_chi.name: Thải Chi
prov_thai_chi.lore: Swamp, forest and tundra at the river's northern mouth around Thải Chi Cốc. Its people grow herbs and gather marsh plants, and the valley's orphans learn their letters in the drying sheds. Poison leeches infest the marsh, and gatherers wrap their legs.

prov_r5_1.name: Sóc Phong Nguyên
prov_r5_1.lore: Flat tundra on the northern coast, scoured bare by the north wind. No one lives here; reindeer cross it in summer and leave before the first snow. A cold spring of water qi rises in its middle.

prov_r5_10.name: Điếu Đài
prov_r5_10.lore: River forest on the lower river, its people fishing from stone terraces on the bank. A spirit vein of soft water qi lies near the river. The drowned abbey of Tĩnh Thủy Quán stands in the woods, its walls still marked by the flood of 700.

prov_r5_11.name: Lư Từ
prov_r5_11.lore: River forest where villagers fish with trained cormorants on the slow reaches. They sell their catch at Đào Thanh. The maples behind the village turn red each autumn.

prov_r5_12.name: Phủ Tạc
prov_r5_12.lore: Inland forest whose villagers are carpenters, building boats, carts and houses for the river towns. Wild oxen graze the clearings. Its carpenters are hired as far as Tùng Gian.

prov_r5_13.name: Mạch Hương
prov_r5_13.lore: River lowland where villagers grow barley and wheat on the flood flats. Its grain goes to the granaries of Lâm Hạ. An old elm wood shelters its fields from the north wind.

prov_r5_14.name: Hoành Độ
prov_r5_14.lore: Low river forest at a crossing of the Nine-Bend River. Its people run a ferry and fish. Lãng Đào takes a share of its fares.

prov_r5_15.name: Giá Ngưu
prov_r5_15.lore: Inland forest and clearings where villagers breed and drive oxen for the river towns' carts. Giant badgers dig their burrows on a knoll nearby. Oxen from here haul the timber down to the river.

prov_r5_16.name: Hà Đê
prov_r5_16.lore: River lowland behind a long earth levee, raised after the flood of 700. Its people farm the flats and mend the levee every spring. A spirit vein of water qi runs beside the river.

prov_r5_17.name: Thủy Xa
prov_r5_17.lore: River forest where villagers lift water to their fields with tall waterwheels. Its people farm and grind grain. The frost-leaf forest behind turns red early.

prov_r5_18.name: Bối Dược
prov_r5_18.lore: Inland hill forest where villagers gather wild herbs and carry them on their backs to Thải Chi Cốc. A spirit vein of wood qi lies under the hill. Herb gatherers come from all over the basin.

prov_r5_19.name: Thạch Lũy
prov_r5_19.lore: Inland forest and hills where villagers build stone walls around their fields. Its people farm and gather firewood. A grey cypress wood climbs the hill.

prov_r5_2.name: Hoang Tự Câu
prov_r5_2.lore: Forest and tundra in the north, with gullies where a temple stood before Tùng Đào came. No one lives here now. A northern birch wood shelters the ruins.

prov_r5_20.name: Tân Lưu
prov_r5_20.lore: River forest on the new course of the river, near the dry bed of Đông Lưu Thành. Tân Lưu Trấn grew on the new current, and its people fish, farm and trade. Children dig for coins on the old bed since the flood of 1198.

prov_r5_21.name: Độc Mộc
prov_r5_21.lore: River forest whose villagers cross the river on a single great log. Its people fish and carve dugout canoes. Ospreys nest on a rock above the river.

prov_r5_22.name: Sài Môn
prov_r5_22.lore: Hill forest where villagers live quietly behind brushwood gates. Its people gather firewood and pine nuts. A cloud pine forest climbs the hill.

prov_r5_23.name: Tùng Lộ
prov_r5_23.lore: Inland hill forest where villagers dig pine truffles with trained pigs. The truffles sell well in Đào Thanh. A forest of tall pines like a thousand pillars rises behind.

prov_r5_24.name: Cung Tiễn
prov_r5_24.lore: Hill forest where villagers make bows and arrows for hunters and Tùng Đào's guards. Its people hunt and craft. Sacred old trees stand on the hill above.

prov_r5_25.name: Thạch Lâu
prov_r5_25.lore: Forest climbing into high mountain near a thousand metres. Its people herd goats and gather herbs. The burned pavilion of Lăng Tiêu Các stands high on the mountain.

prov_r5_26.name: Ma Bố
prov_r5_26.lore: High forest where villagers grow hemp and weave cloth. Its people farm and weave. Hemlock forest climbs the mountain above.

prov_r5_27.name: Lâm Khẩu
prov_r5_27.lore: Forest climbing into hills, its village at the forest's mouth. Its people hunt and gather. Sabre-toothed cats roam a ridge nearby.

prov_r5_28.name: Vân Biên
prov_r5_28.lore: High forest and rock near the clouds. Its people herd goats and gather herbs. Hawks nest on a crag, and the cliff-cut halls of Đoạn Vân Viện stand broken nearby.

prov_r5_29.name: Hổ Bối Lĩnh
prov_r5_29.lore: High mountain and forest around Hổ Khiếu Cương. No one lives here now; the tiger and the thin ore drove the miners out. Tùng Đào's riders go around the ridges, not over them.

prov_r5_3.name: Thương Lô Trạch
prov_r5_3.lore: Swamp and forest on the northern coast, thick with grey reeds. No one lives here. Mud dragons hold its shoals.

prov_r5_30.name: Tầng Điền
prov_r5_30.lore: High forest and rock where villagers farm terraces on the slopes. Its people grow barley and buckwheat. The sealed abbey of Cô Hạc Quán stands high above.

prov_r5_31.name: Lẫm Phong Lĩnh
prov_r5_31.lore: The highest mountains of the basin, rising to nearly two thousand metres. No one lives here but miners. From its peak the whole river can be seen.

prov_r5_4.name: Tùng Tâm
prov_r5_4.lore: Inland pine forest in the north of the basin. Its people split resinous pine heartwood for torches. Porcupines roam a wood nearby.

prov_r5_5.name: Ô Bồng
prov_r5_5.lore: Forest and swamp on the coast, where villagers fish from boats with black awnings. Its people fish and gather reeds. A flooded wood lies behind the village.

prov_r5_6.name: Băng Thảo Hoang
prov_r5_6.lore: Tundra on the northern coast, its grass frozen most of the year. No one lives here. A vein of water qi lies under the ice.

prov_r5_7.name: Bạch Thạch
prov_r5_7.lore: Forest on the coast, its village built of white stone. Its people fish and quarry. Blue martens roam the woods.

prov_r5_8.name: Đà Công
prov_r5_8.lore: River forest where villagers serve as helmsmen for Lãng Đào's ferries. Its people know every bend of the river. Weeping willows line its banks.

prov_r5_9.name: Ngọa Ngưu
prov_r5_9.lore: River forest named for a hill shaped like a resting ox. Its people farm and fish. The fallen gate of Phân Thủy Môn stands in the woods.

prov_lang_dao_spirit_vein_1.name: Tẩy Sa Tuyền
prov_lang_dao_spirit_vein_1.look: A clear spring bubbles up through white sand in the woods behind the gate of hulls, its pool ringed with oar blades driven into the ground.
prov_lang_dao_spirit_vein_1.lore: A spirit vein of Water qi feeds the spring. Lãng Đào's disciples wash their oars in it before a voyage and plant an old oar beside it when they retire.

prov_lang_dao_ruin_2.name: Phá Chu Trấn
prov_lang_dao_ruin_2.look: On the shore, rotted piers and the hulls of boats lie broken in the sand, among the stone footings of a small town.
prov_lang_dao_ruin_2.lore: The boatmen's town where the families of the river fought over landings. In 786 a feud ended with half the town burned, and the survivors were among those who banded together as Lãng Đào Môn four years later.

prov_p108_forest_1.name: Thâm Tuyết Lâm
prov_p108_forest_1.look: A fir forest where the snow lies deeper than a man is tall all winter, only the treetops showing above the drifts.
prov_p108_forest_1.lore: The villagers of Tuyết Ốc tunnel into it for firewood. Hunters say bears and stranger beasts sleep under the snow here until the thaw.

prov_p109_forest_1.name: Dã Mai Lâm
prov_p109_forest_1.look: A wood of wild plum trees on the slope above the village, their red blossoms opening through the snow.
prov_p109_forest_1.lore: The villagers of Hàn Mai say the plums grew from the seeds of their own tree. The swordsmen of Ngạo Tuyết Phái train among them in the blossom season.

prov_p109_minor_seat_p.name: Ngạo Tuyết Phái
prov_p109_minor_seat_p.look: A small school of grey-tiled halls among wild plums on a slope above the river, its practice yard ringed with plum trees.
prov_p109_minor_seat_p.lore: Ngạo Tuyết Phái is a small school of sword cultivators sworn to Tùng Đào Cung, founded in 1105 by a swordsman who learned his art watching the plum bloom through the snow. Its plum-blossom sword forms are quick and light.

sect.name: Ngạo Tuyết Phái
sect.craft: sword cultivation (kiếm tu); plum-blossom sword forms

prov_p110_beast_lair_1.name: Lang Hồi Cương
prov_p110_beast_lair_1.look: A forested knoll above the river, its moss cut by wolf trails and its foot littered with gnawed deer bones.
prov_p110_beast_lair_1.lore: Grey wolves have come back to this knoll in the centuries since the white wolf king fell. The villagers of Bạch Lang say the year they leave the den's boulders grey, the wolves will come down.

prov_p33_spirit_vein_1.name: Đào Âm Mạch
prov_p33_spirit_vein_1.look: A pine-covered hill above the city where the wind in the crowns roars like surf, and the ground underfoot trembles faintly with it.
prov_p33_spirit_vein_1.lore: A spirit vein of Wood qi runs under the hill. The townsfolk of Đào Thanh climb up on windy evenings to hear the pines.

prov_p47_forest_1.name: Bạch Dương Lâm
prov_p47_forest_1.look: A wood of tall white poplars on the dunes behind the sand flats, their leaves flickering silver in the sea wind.
prov_p47_forest_1.lore: The poplars hold the dunes against the wind and keep the sand off the washing cradles. The gold-washers gather firewood here.

prov_p62_beast_lair_1.name: Cự Miết Chử
prov_p62_beast_lair_1.look: Muddy shoals in a slow bend of the river, where flat leathery shells as wide as doors bask in the sun and slide into the water at a footstep.
prov_p62_beast_lair_1.lore: Giant softshell turtles live in the bend and snap at the oars of passing boats. Hà Bạn's fishermen go wide of the shoals, and alchemists pay well for a shell.

prov_p62_ruin_2.name: Cựu Hà Trấn
prov_p62_ruin_2.look: On a dry rise, the silted streets of a small town lie under grass, with a stone landing stair that ends in a meadow.
prov_p62_ruin_2.lore: A town on the old course of the river, left dry when the river changed course. Its people moved to the new bank, and Hà Bạn Trấn grew there.

prov_p63_beast_lair_1.name: Thử Vương Cương
prov_p63_beast_lair_1.look: A knoll riddled with rat holes the width of a man's arm, its grass stripped and grain husks heaped at the burrow mouths.
prov_p63_beast_lair_1.lore: Giant rats live here and raid the granaries of Lâm Hạ whenever a staddle cracks. The town's rat-catchers hunt them with terriers and smoke.

prov_thai_chi_beast_lair_1.name: Độc Điệt Trạch
prov_thai_chi_beast_lair_1.look: A cold marsh of black water and grey reeds where leeches as long as a hand ripple through the shallows toward any footstep.
prov_thai_chi_beast_lair_1.lore: Poison leeches infest the marsh, and their bite leaves a numb welt for days. Thải Chi's herb gatherers wrap their legs in oiled cloth, and the valley's alchemists collect the leeches for a blood-thinning draught.

prov_r5_1_spirit_vein_1.name: Hàn Tinh Tuyền
prov_r5_1_spirit_vein_1.look: A cold spring in the open tundra, its still pool so clear that on winter nights it holds the stars like a second sky.
prov_r5_1_spirit_vein_1.lore: A spirit vein of Water qi feeds the spring. Tùng Đào's disciples come in summer, the only season the walk is possible.

prov_r5_10_village_1.name: Điếu Đài Thôn
prov_r5_10_village_1.look: A river village whose bank is stepped with flat stone terraces, each with a fisher sitting on it and a long rod over the current.
prov_r5_10_village_1.lore: Each family owns its own terrace and passes it down with the house. The village sells its catch at Đào Thanh, and the oldest terrace is said to be older than the levees.

prov_r5_10_spirit_vein_2.name: Nhu Thủy Mạch
prov_r5_10_spirit_vein_2.look: A hollow near the river where a spring seeps through moss into a pool so soft that stones on its bed are worn round as eggs.
prov_r5_10_spirit_vein_2.lore: A spirit vein of Water qi runs here, gentle and slow. Tùng Đào's water cultivators come to learn patience at it, and the drowned monks of Tĩnh Thủy Quán once did the same.

prov_r5_10_ruin_3.name: Tĩnh Thủy Quán
prov_r5_10_ruin_3.look: In the woods, the mud-filled halls of an abbey stand with water marks high on their walls.
prov_r5_10_ruin_3.lore: A small sect that cultivated the stillness of water. The great flood of 700 drowned it along with three villages, and the survivors went to Tùng Đào two years later.

prov_r5_11_village_1.name: Lư Từ Thôn
prov_r5_11_village_1.look: A river village of grey roofs where black cormorants perch on the gunwales of narrow boats, rings around their necks.
prov_r5_11_village_1.lore: Its people fish the slow reaches with trained cormorants that bring back fish they cannot swallow. They sell their catch at Đào Thanh and give each bird the seventh fish.

prov_r5_11_forest_2.name: Phong Thụ Lâm
prov_r5_11_forest_2.look: A maple forest behind the village that turns red in autumn.
prov_r5_11_forest_2.lore: The villagers tap maple sap in spring and boil it into syrup for the river towns. Cormorant fishers judge the autumn fish run by how red the leaves have turned.

prov_r5_12_village_1.name: Phủ Tạc Thôn
prov_r5_12_village_1.look: A forest village of open-sided workshops where boat ribs, cartwheels and roof beams lie half-shaped in the wood shavings.
prov_r5_12_village_1.lore: Its carpenters build boats, carts and houses for the river towns and are hired as far as Tùng Gian. Each apprentice carves his own mallet before he may touch a chisel.

prov_r5_12_beast_lair_2.name: Dã Ngưu Nguyên
prov_r5_12_beast_lair_2.look: A broad clearing in the forest, its grass grazed short and churned by hooves, where shaggy dark oxen stand in a wary herd.
prov_r5_12_beast_lair_2.lore: Wild oxen graze here and charge anyone who comes between them and their calves. Hunters of Phủ Tạc take one or two in winter, and the carpenters buy their horn for glue.

prov_r5_13_village_1.name: Mạch Hương Thôn
prov_r5_13_village_1.look: A river village of grey roofs among fields of barley and wheat on the flood flats, with threshing floors by every house.
prov_r5_13_village_1.lore: Its people sow the flats as soon as the spring flood drains and send their grain to the granaries of Lâm Hạ. At harvest the whole bend smells of bread.

prov_r5_13_forest_2.name: Du Âm Lâm
prov_r5_13_forest_2.look: A strip of old elms between the fields and the north wind, their broad crowns throwing deep shade.
prov_r5_13_forest_2.lore: The elms shelter the fields of Mạch Hương from the wind. In hard years the villagers eat the young elm seeds, and they call the wood their second granary.

prov_r5_14_village_1.name: Hoành Độ Thôn
prov_r5_14_village_1.look: A river village where a broad flat ferry hauls across the river on a rope, and carts wait in line at the landing.
prov_r5_14_village_1.lore: Its people run the ferry across the Nine-Bend River here and fish between crossings. Lãng Đào takes a share of the fares and keeps the rope in repair.

prov_r5_14_forest_2.name: Hắc Hoa Lâm
prov_r5_14_forest_2.look: A damp riverside wood of dark-barked birches, their trunks grey-black and shaggy with curling bark.
prov_r5_14_forest_2.lore: Black birch bark is stripped here for roofing the riverside houses. The ferrymen cut their poles from its straight young trees.

prov_r5_15_village_1.name: Giá Ngưu Thôn
prov_r5_15_village_1.look: A village of ox pens and yoke sheds in a forest clearing, its lanes deep in hoof-churned mud.
prov_r5_15_village_1.lore: Its people breed and drive oxen for the river towns' carts. Oxen from here haul the timber down to the river.

prov_r5_15_beast_lair_2.name: Cự Hoan Cương
prov_r5_15_beast_lair_2.look: A knoll dug full of badger burrows, their mouths ringed with heaps of fresh earth.
prov_r5_15_beast_lair_2.lore: Giant badgers dig here and raid the ox feed. Their burrows can break an ox's leg.

prov_r5_16_village_1.name: Hà Đê Thôn
prov_r5_16_village_1.look: A village behind a long earth levee, its houses below the level of the river in flood.
prov_r5_16_village_1.lore: Its people farm the flats and mend the levee every spring. The levee was raised after the flood of 700.

prov_r5_16_spirit_vein_2.name: Bích Lưu Mạch
prov_r5_16_spirit_vein_2.look: A green pool beside the river, fed by a current that runs clear and jade-green even when the river beside it is brown with flood.
prov_r5_16_spirit_vein_2.lore: A spirit vein of Water qi runs here, and the villagers of Hà Đê say it never floods. Tùng Đào's disciples cultivate on the levee above it.

prov_r5_17_village_1.name: Thủy Xa Thôn
prov_r5_17_village_1.look: A river village where tall bamboo waterwheels creak on the bank, lifting buckets of water into wooden troughs that run to the fields.
prov_r5_17_village_1.lore: Its people lift river water to their fields with the wheels and grind grain with a smaller wheel by the mill. Each wheel is rebuilt every ten years from the same pattern.

prov_r5_17_forest_2.name: Sương Diệp Lâm
prov_r5_17_forest_2.look: A wood of oak and maple behind the village whose leaves turn red with the first frost, weeks before the rest of the river.
prov_r5_17_forest_2.lore: The villagers watch it to know the season: when its leaves turn early, they say, the winter will be hard. Its fallen oak wood feeds the mill fires.

prov_r5_18_village_1.name: Bối Dược Thôn
prov_r5_18_village_1.look: A hill village where tall carrying baskets hang by every door and herbs dry in bundles from the eaves.
prov_r5_18_village_1.lore: Its people gather wild herbs on the hills and carry them on their backs down to Thải Chi Cốc. Herb gatherers come from all over the basin.

prov_r5_18_spirit_vein_2.name: Bách Thảo Mạch
prov_r5_18_spirit_vein_2.look: A hillside clearing so thick with herbs of every kind that its air smells bitter and sweet at once.
prov_r5_18_spirit_vein_2.lore: A spirit vein of Wood qi feeds the herbs, and plants grow here that grow nowhere else in the basin. Thải Chi Cốc's alchemists prize them and send a gatherer each spring.

prov_r5_19_village_1.name: Thạch Lũy Thôn
prov_r5_19_village_1.look: A village with stone walls around its fields, built from the stones they cleared.
prov_r5_19_village_1.lore: Its people build stone walls from the stones they clear. They farm and gather firewood.

prov_r5_19_forest_2.name: Thương Bách Lâm
prov_r5_19_forest_2.look: A wood of grey-green cypresses on the hill above the village, their scent sharp in the cold air.
prov_r5_19_forest_2.lore: Cypress from here is used for coffins and shrine beams. The villagers of Thạch Lũy bury their dead under its trees.

prov_r5_2_forest_1.name: Bắc Hoa Lâm
prov_r5_2_forest_1.look: A thin birch wood on the tundra's edge, its trees bent low by the north wind and its floor white with lichen.
prov_r5_2_forest_1.lore: The birches shelter the ruins of Tuyết Thiền Tự. Reindeer herders camp here in summer and strip bark for their tents.

prov_r5_2_ruin_2.name: Tuyết Thiền Tự
prov_r5_2_ruin_2.look: In a gully, the stone halls of a temple stand roofless under snow.
prov_r5_2_ruin_2.lore: A small sect of monks who meditated in the snow. In the hard winter of 261 most of them starved, and the last walked south to Tùng Đào Cung the next spring.

prov_r5_20_town_1.name: Tân Lưu Trấn
prov_r5_20_town_1.look: A river town on the new course of the river, its wharves busy with boats.
prov_r5_20_town_1.lore: It grew on the new current after the river left Đông Lưu Thành. Its people fish, farm and trade.

prov_r5_20_forest_2.name: Cựu Đạo Lâm
prov_r5_20_forest_2.look: A long, narrow wood of willow and alder growing in a winding line across the meadow, following the dry bed of the old river.
prov_r5_20_forest_2.lore: The trees took root on the bed the river left in 281, and their line still shows its old bends. Since the flood of 1198, children from Tân Lưu dig among the roots for coins of Đông Lưu Thành.

prov_r5_21_village_1.name: Độc Mộc Thôn
prov_r5_21_village_1.look: A river village on both banks, joined by one huge pine trunk laid across a narrow, rocky stretch of the river, with dugout canoes pulled up below.
prov_r5_21_village_1.lore: Its people cross the river on the log and carve dugout canoes from single trunks. When the log rots, the whole village goes up the hill together to fell the next one.

prov_r5_21_beast_lair_2.name: Ngư Ưng Đài
prov_r5_21_beast_lair_2.look: A rock above the river where ospreys nest, their great stick nests piled on its ledges.
prov_r5_21_beast_lair_2.lore: Ospreys nest here and fish the river. The villagers watch them for the fish runs.

prov_r5_22_village_1.name: Sài Môn Thôn
prov_r5_22_village_1.look: A quiet hill village of thatched houses, each with a gate of woven brushwood and a pine-nut tree in the yard.
prov_r5_22_village_1.lore: Its people gather firewood and pine nuts and keep to themselves. Retired outer disciples of Tùng Đào sometimes settle here to grow old in quiet.

prov_r5_22_forest_2.name: Vân Tùng Lâm
prov_r5_22_forest_2.look: A pine forest high on the hill, its crowns lost in low cloud on most mornings and dripping with mist.
prov_r5_22_forest_2.lore: Tùng Đào's disciples climb here to cultivate in the mist among the pines. The villagers of Sài Môn gather pine nuts only on its lower edge.

prov_r5_23_village_1.name: Tùng Lộ Thôn
prov_r5_23_village_1.look: A hill village with truffle pigs in pens.
prov_r5_23_village_1.lore: Its people dig pine truffles with trained pigs. The truffles sell well in Đào Thanh.

prov_r5_23_forest_2.name: Thiên Trụ Lâm
prov_r5_23_forest_2.look: A forest of tall, straight, branchless pines standing like the pillars of an endless hall, their crowns far overhead.
prov_r5_23_forest_2.lore: The pines are so straight that Tùng Đào's builders once came here for hall pillars, and the stumps of that cutting still show. The truffle diggers of Tùng Lộ work its roots.

prov_r5_24_village_1.name: Cung Tiễn Thôn
prov_r5_24_village_1.look: A hill village of bowyers, bow staves seasoning under every roof.
prov_r5_24_village_1.lore: Its people make bows and arrows for hunters and Tùng Đào's guards. They hunt too.

prov_r5_24_forest_2.name: Thần Mộc Lâm
prov_r5_24_forest_2.look: On the hilltop, a grove of colossal old trees whose trunks are wrapped with red cords and hung with small votive boards.
prov_r5_24_forest_2.lore: The bowyers of Cung Tiễn hold the trees sacred and never cut them, and they bring each new bow here to be blessed before it is sold. They say an arrow fletched with a feather found in the grove never misses.

prov_r5_25_village_1.name: Thạch Lâu Thôn
prov_r5_25_village_1.look: A mountain village of goat pens and stone huts gathered under a squat stone watchtower with a fire basket on top.
prov_r5_25_village_1.lore: Its people herd goats and gather herbs on the high slopes. The tower is lit when the green oxen come down the valley, so the herders can drive their flocks clear.

prov_r5_25_beast_lair_2.name: Thanh Ngưu Cốc
prov_r5_25_beast_lair_2.look: A high valley of mountain meadow where massive oxen with dark green-tinged coats graze among the boulders.
prov_r5_25_beast_lair_2.lore: Spirit oxen live here, gentle unless their calves are threatened; then they charge like a landslide. Herbalists gather the rare grasses they leave ungrazed.

prov_r5_25_ruin_3.name: Lăng Tiêu Các
prov_r5_25_ruin_3.gloss: Pavilion That Rises to the Sky
prov_r5_25_ruin_3.look: High on the mountain, the burned shell of a pavilion stands against the sky.
prov_r5_25_ruin_3.lore: A small sect of alchemists. A fire in its pill hall in 1066 burned the pavilion, and its disciples scattered.

prov_r5_26_village_1.name: Ma Bố Thôn
prov_r5_26_village_1.look: A high village of narrow hemp fields and stone houses where looms clack in every doorway and retting pits steam in the stream.
prov_r5_26_village_1.lore: Its people grow hemp on the slopes and weave a coarse, hard-wearing cloth for sails and sacks. They sell it at Đào Thanh.

prov_r5_26_forest_2.name: Thiết Sam Lâm
prov_r5_26_forest_2.look: A dark hemlock forest climbing the mountain, its drooping branches heavy with snow half the year.
prov_r5_26_forest_2.lore: Hemlock wood here is hard and does not split, and the weavers of Ma Bố make their loom frames from it. Few go deeper than the woodcutters' paths.

prov_r5_27_village_1.name: Lâm Khẩu Thôn
prov_r5_27_village_1.look: A village of log houses at the mouth of a forest valley, a tall palisade on the forest side.
prov_r5_27_village_1.lore: Its people hunt and gather in the valley behind. They keep the palisade high because of the sabre-toothed cats on the ridge.

prov_r5_27_beast_lair_2.name: Kiếm Xỉ Lĩnh
prov_r5_27_beast_lair_2.look: A forested ridge whose trunks are scored with deep claw marks, and deer bones lie cracked in its hollows.
prov_r5_27_beast_lair_2.lore: Sabre-toothed cats den on the ridge and hunt deer in the valley below. Hunters of Lâm Khẩu go in groups of six, and a fang from here buys a cow.

prov_r5_28_village_1.name: Vân Biên Thôn
prov_r5_28_village_1.look: A high village of stone huts on a shelf above the forest, where the clouds often lie below the houses like a white sea.
prov_r5_28_village_1.lore: Its people herd goats and gather herbs on the crags. They guard their kids against the hawks of the crag above.

prov_r5_28_beast_lair_2.name: Ưng Sào Nhai
prov_r5_28_beast_lair_2.look: A grey crag above the village, its ledges crowned with stick nests and whitened by droppings.
prov_r5_28_beast_lair_2.lore: Great hawks nest on the crag and take young goats from the slopes. Vân Biên's herders climb up each spring to take chicks for taming, and the hawks remember them.

prov_r5_28_ruin_3.name: Đoạn Vân Viện
prov_r5_28_ruin_3.look: On a cliff, the cut halls of an academy lie broken.
prov_r5_28_ruin_3.lore: A small sect that cut its halls into the cliff. An earthquake in 1134 broke them, and the survivors went to Tùng Đào.

prov_r5_29_mine_1.name: Hổ Văn Khoáng
prov_r5_29_mine_1.look: A mine in banded rock like a tiger's stripes, its adit now dark and silent.
prov_r5_29_mine_1.lore: The mine dug banded iron ore. The tiger of Hổ Khiếu Cương drove the miners out.

prov_r5_29_ruin_2.name: Thạch Khẩu Trấn
prov_r5_29_ruin_2.look: A miners' town in ruins on the mountain, its stone houses roofless.
prov_r5_29_ruin_2.lore: The miners' town of the tiger-stripe mine. The ore ran thin and the tiger took miners, and it emptied in 1161.

prov_r5_3_beast_lair_1.name: Nê Giao Chử
prov_r5_3_beast_lair_1.look: Low mud shoals among grey reeds where long, ridged backs lie half sunk like logs, and the mud is scored with drag marks.
prov_r5_3_beast_lair_1.lore: Mud dragons (giao) lurk in the shoals and drag deer and stray reindeer down into the mud. No one cuts reeds within sight of them, and the coast fishers row wide of the marsh mouth.

prov_r5_30_village_1.name: Tầng Điền Thôn
prov_r5_30_village_1.look: A high village under stair-stepped terraces of barley and buckwheat, held up by dry-stone walls that climb the whole slope.
prov_r5_30_village_1.lore: Its people farm the terraces and rebuild a wall or two each spring after the frost heaves them. They carry earth up in baskets to replace what the rains wash down.

prov_r5_30_forest_2.name: Quải Đài Lâm
prov_r5_30_forest_2.look: A high, misty forest of old firs hung so thick with grey-green lichen that the branches look like bearded old men.
prov_r5_30_forest_2.lore: The lichen grows only where the air is clean and damp, and alchemists of Thải Chi Cốc buy it for wound salves. The villagers of Tầng Điền gather it in autumn.

prov_r5_30_ruin_3.name: Cô Hạc Quán
prov_r5_30_ruin_3.look: A sealed abbey high on the mountain, its main door still closed under a faded seal.
prov_r5_30_ruin_3.lore: A small sect of hermits. Its abbot died in closed-door cultivation in 1010, and no one could break his seal; the disciples scattered.

prov_r5_31_peak_1.name: Vọng Xuyên Phong
prov_r5_31_peak_1.look: The highest peak of the basin, a bare grey summit near two thousand metres, from which the whole river shines in its nine bends.
prov_r5_31_peak_1.lore: A peak of Metal qi, cold and sharp. Tùng Đào's disciples climb it to cultivate, and river pilots say a man who has counted all nine bends from its top will never lose his way on the water.

prov_r5_31_mine_2.name: Ngân Tuyết Khoáng
prov_r5_31_mine_2.look: A timbered adit high on bare rock, its spoil heaps glittering with silver ore under the snow.
prov_r5_31_mine_2.lore: The mine digs silver from the high rock in the short summer and closes in winter. Tùng Đào posts a guard on the ore road down to Đào Thanh.

prov_r5_4_village_1.name: Tùng Tâm Thôn
prov_r5_4_village_1.look: A pine forest village where bundles of split, resin-soaked heartwood stand drying against every wall.
prov_r5_4_village_1.lore: Its people split the resinous heartwood of fallen pines into torches that burn for hours. They sell them at Đào Sa for the night washers.

prov_r5_4_beast_lair_2.name: Tiễn Trư Lâm
prov_r5_4_beast_lair_2.look: A wood of gnawed pines, bark stripped in rings and the ground scattered with long black-and-white quills.
prov_r5_4_beast_lair_2.lore: Porcupines as big as dogs live here and kill the young pines by gnawing their bark. Their quills are gathered for arrows and fish lures.

prov_r5_5_village_1.name: Ô Bồng Thôn
prov_r5_5_village_1.look: A coastal village of reed houses where narrow boats with arched black-tarred awnings lie in rows at the water's edge.
prov_r5_5_village_1.lore: Its people fish the coast and the marsh channels from the awninged boats and sleep in them in the fishing season. They gather reeds for thatch and mats.

prov_r5_5_forest_2.name: Tẩm Thủy Lâm
prov_r5_5_forest_2.look: A swamp wood of alder and willow standing knee-deep in still brown water, the trunks stained dark to the flood line.
prov_r5_5_forest_2.lore: The villagers of Ô Bồng pole their boats between the trees and set eel traps among the roots. In spring the water rises to the low branches.

prov_r5_6_spirit_vein_1.name: Băng Lưu Huyệt
prov_r5_6_spirit_vein_1.look: A hollow in the tundra where a frozen stream of blue ice pours out of the ground and spreads in a fan that never melts.
prov_r5_6_spirit_vein_1.lore: A spirit vein of Water qi rises here, so cold it freezes its own water as it flows. Tùng Đào's disciples sit on the ice to temper their bodies in the summer.

prov_r5_7_village_1.name: Bạch Thạch Thôn
prov_r5_7_village_1.look: A coastal village of white stone houses on a pale rocky shore, boats drawn up between the quarry heaps.
prov_r5_7_village_1.lore: Its people fish and quarry the white stone of the shore, which goes by boat to Đào Thanh for steps and quays. The whole village glows at sunset.

prov_r5_7_beast_lair_2.name: Thanh Điêu Lâm
prov_r5_7_beast_lair_2.look: A coastal pine wood where blue-grey martens flicker through the branches, and stripped pine cones litter the ground.
prov_r5_7_beast_lair_2.lore: Blue martens hunt squirrels here, and their pelts are prized in the winter markets. Trappers of Bạch Thạch take them only in deep winter, when the fur is thickest.

prov_r5_8_village_1.name: Đà Công Thôn
prov_r5_8_village_1.look: A river village of helmsmen, steering oars racked by every door.
prov_r5_8_village_1.lore: Its people serve as helmsmen for Lãng Đào's ferries. They know every bend of the river.

prov_r5_8_forest_2.name: Thùy Dương Lâm
prov_r5_8_forest_2.look: A wood of weeping willows along the river bank, their long branches trailing in the current.
prov_r5_8_forest_2.lore: The willows hold the bank against the spring floods. The helmsmen of Đà Công rest in their shade between voyages and cut withies here for baskets.

prov_r5_9_village_1.name: Ngọa Ngưu Thôn
prov_r5_9_village_1.look: A river village under a low hill shaped exactly like an ox lying down, its fields reaching to the bank.
prov_r5_9_village_1.lore: Its people farm and fish, and they leave a bundle of hay on the hill's head each new year. They say the day the ox rises, the river will flood.

prov_r5_9_forest_2.name: Hồi Thanh Lâm
prov_r5_9_forest_2.look: A pine forest in a ring of low hills, where every call comes back twice, a little later each time.
prov_r5_9_forest_2.lore: Sounds echo strangely among its trees. The villagers of Ngọa Ngưu come on the night of the dead to call their dead by name and listen for the answer.

prov_r5_9_ruin_3.name: Phân Thủy Môn
prov_r5_9_ruin_3.look: In the woods, the fallen gate of a sect.
prov_r5_9_ruin_3.lore: A small sect of boatmen. Its boats sank in a feud in 788, and the survivors joined Lãng Đào Môn two years later.
